segments.arabic:
١٢٣٠٨- أم يحيى:
استدركها أبو موسى.
وقد «١» ذكرناها في ترجمة زيدة «٢» أو زائدة جارية عمر ... يعني في الزّاء المنقوطة من أسماء النساء.
ولم يذكر هناك ما يدل على أنّ لها صحبة، وإنما أورد لها رواية عن عائشة، فقيل:
عن أم يحيى، عن عائشة. وقيل عن أم نجيح، عن عائشة. وباللَّه التوفيق «٣» .
(١) في هـ-: وقال.
(٢) في أ، هـ-: بريدة.
(٣) ثبت في (أ) . آخر النساء من الإصابة، وبالنسخة المنقولة منها في أخرى ما نصه: وهو آخر ما وجدته بخط شيخ الإسلام، حافظ العصر أبي الفضل ابن حجر العسقلاني أمير المؤمنين في الحديث مصنف الكتاب، تغمّده اللَّه بالرحمة والرضوان، وأسكنه فسيح الجنان. وقد بقي عليه المبهمات، وقيد منها كثيرا، ولكني لم أظفر به الآن، وعسى أن أظفر به إن شاء اللَّه تعالى، وقد مشقت الكتاب جمعية في مدّة يسيرة جدّا من خط مؤلفه. وصلى اللَّه على أشرف خلقه سيدنا محمد وآله وصحبه وسلم تسليما كثيرا آمين. وكان الفراغ من تكملة هذا الكتاب نهار الجمعة المبارك حادي عشر ربيع الأول سنة ثلاث وثمانين وألف من الهجرة النبويّة على صاحبها أفضل الصلاة وأزكى التحية على يد الحقير الراجي عفو ربه القدير السيد عطا اللَّه ابن المرحوم الحاج أحمد العقاد غفر اللَّه لهما آمين. وثبت في (ع) وباللَّه التوفيق، آخر كتاب النساء من الإصابة، وهو آخر ما وجد بخط العلّامة شيخ الإسلام حافظ العصر ابن حجر، مصنّف الكتاب، تغمّده اللَّه بالرحمة والرضوان، وأسكنه فسيح الجنان، وكان الفراغ من كتابة هذه النسخة المباركة في يوم السبت المبارك خامس عشر شعبان المعظم قدره من شهور سنة ثلاث وتسعين وألف من الهجرة النبويّة، على صاحبها أفضل الصلاة والسلام على يد كاتبه العبد الفقير راجي عفو ربّه. عبد الرحمن بن موسى بن علي الشيخوني الشوبري، غفر اللَّه له ولوالديه، ولجميع المسلمين آمين.
segments.english:
12308—Umm Yahya:

Abu Musa added her as an omitted entry.

We have (1) mentioned her in the entry on Zayda (2), or Za'ida, the slave woman of Umar … that is, under the dotted letter zay among the names of women.

Nothing mentioned there indicates that she was a Companion; rather, only a report transmitted by her from Aisha was cited. Thus it was said:

“From Umm Yahya, from Aisha”; and it was also said, “From Umm Najih, from Aisha.” With Allah is all success. (3)

(1) In manuscript H-: “And he said.”

(2) In manuscripts A and H-: “Burayda.”

(3) The following appears in manuscript A: “End of the women’s entries of al-Isabah.” In another copy transcribed from it, the following text appears: “This is the last of what I found in the handwriting of the Shaykh al-Islam, the leading hadith master of the age, Abu al-Fadl ibn Hajar al-Asqalani, Commander of the Faithful in hadith and author of this book. May Allah envelop him in mercy and good pleasure and lodge him in the spacious gardens of Paradise. The anonymous entries remained for him to complete, and he had recorded many of them, but I have not come upon that material at present. Perhaps I shall come upon it, if Allah Most High wills. I copied out the entire book in a very short time from its author’s handwriting. May Allah bless the most noble of His creation, our master Muhammad, and his family and Companions, and grant them abundant peace. Amen. The completion of this book took place during the blessed daytime of Friday, the eleventh of Rabi I in the year 1083 after the Prophet’s Hijra—may the finest blessings and purest greetings be upon him—at the hand of the humble one who hopes for the pardon of his all-powerful Lord, al-Sayyid Ata Allah ibn the late al-Hajj Ahmad al-Aqqad. May Allah forgive them both. Amen.”

The following appears in manuscript Ayn: “With Allah is all success. End of the Book of Women from al-Isabah. This is the last of what was found in the handwriting of the learned Shaykh al-Islam and leading hadith master of the age, Abu al-Fadl ibn Hajar al-Asqalani, author of this book. May Allah envelop him in mercy and good pleasure and lodge him in the spacious gardens of Paradise. The copying of this blessed manuscript was completed on the blessed Saturday, the fifteenth of the greatly honored month of Sha'ban, in the year 1093 after the Prophet’s Hijra—may the finest blessings and peace be upon him—at the hand of its copyist, the poor servant who hopes for the pardon of his Lord, Abd al-Rahman ibn Musa ibn Ali al-Shaykhuni al-Shawbari. May Allah forgive him, his parents, and all Muslims. Amen.”

segments.arabic:
. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
والحمد للَّه ربّ العالمين، وصلّى اللَّه على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وصحبه وسلّم تسليما كثيرا آمين. وثبت في (ل) وباللَّه التوفيق آخر كتاب النساء من الإصابة، وفي النسخة المنقول منها ما نصّه. هذا آخر ما وجدته بخط شيخ الإسلام، حافظ العصر أبي الفضل بن حجر العسقلاني، أمير المؤمنين في الحديث، مصنّف الكتاب، تغمّده اللَّه بالرحمة والرضوان، وأسكنه فسيح الجنان نحن وإياه ولمن نظر فيه ... آمين- آمين- آمين. وثبت في (د) تمّ الفراغ في إتمام هذا الكتاب بعون اللَّه الملك الوهّاب على أضعف الكتاب السيد الحاج محمد طالب ابن السيد محمد أسد الوندي في أربعة وعشرين يوما خلت من شهر جمادى الثاني من شهور سنة ألف ومائة وأربعة وثلاثين في هجرة من له الشرف والعزّ والتمكين، وصلى اللَّه على سيدنا محمد وعلى آله وصحبه الكرام الطاهرين، والحمد للَّه ربّ العالمين. وثبت في (ت) وباللَّه التوفيق، آخر كتاب النساء من الإصابة، وبالتحقيق المنقول منها ما نصه، وهو آخر ما وجدته بخط شيخ الإسلام، حافظ العصر أبي الفضل بن حجر العسقلاني، أمير المؤمنين في الحديث، مصنّف الكتاب، تغمّده اللَّه بالرحمة والرضوان، وأسكنه فسيح الجنان، وقد بقي عليه المبهمات، وقيد كثيرا منهما، والكنى لم أظفر به إلى الآن، وعسى أن نخرجه إن شاء اللَّه تعالى. وقد مشقت الكتاب جميعه في مدّه يسيرة جدا من خط مؤلفه، وصلّى اللَّه على أشرف خلقه سيدنا محمد وآله وصحبه وسلم تسليما كثيرا آمين. وكان الفراغ من كتابتها يوم السبت المبارك ثالث عشرة من شهر ذي الحجة من شهور سنة تسع وعشرين ومائة وألف بعد الهجرة النبويّة على مشرفها أفضل الصلاة والسلام. وكتبه بنفسه العبد الفقير إلى عفو ربّه الفقير محمد بن الشيخ الفاضل الشيخ حاضر ابن المرحوم الشيخ عبد اللَّه بن المرحوم الشيخ أحمد الدمهوحي الشافعيّ، غفر اللَّه له ولوالده.
segments.english:
. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .

And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds. May Allah bless our master Muhammad and his family and Companions, and grant them abundant peace. Amen.

It is recorded in (L): “And through Allah comes success. Here ends the Book of the Women from al-Isabah.” In the copy from which it was transcribed, the wording is: “This is the last of what I found in the handwriting of Shaykh al-Islam, the hadith master of the age, Abu al-Fadl ibn Hajar al-Asqalani, Commander of the Faithful in Hadith and author of the book—may Allah envelop him in mercy and good pleasure and lodge him in the spacious gardens of Paradise; we and him, and for whoever looks into it ... Amen—Amen—Amen.”

It is recorded in (D): “The completion of this book was finished, with the aid of Allah, the King, the Bestower, by the weakest of scribes, al-Sayyid al-Hajj Muhammad Talib ibn al-Sayyid Muhammad Asad al-Wandi, when twenty-four days had elapsed of the month of Jumada II, in the year 1134 of the Hijra of him to whom belong honor, might, and established authority. May Allah bless our master Muhammad and his noble, pure family and Companions. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.”

It is recorded in (T): “And through Allah comes success. Here ends the Book of the Women from al-Isabah. And, upon verification, the text copied from it is as follows: ‘This is the last of what I found in the handwriting of Shaykh al-Islam, the hadith master of the age, Abu al-Fadl ibn Hajar al-Asqalani, Commander of the Faithful in Hadith and author of the book—may Allah envelop him in mercy and good pleasure and lodge him in the spacious gardens of Paradise. The Unidentified Persons still remained for him, and he had recorded a great deal concerning “the two of them”; as for the Kunyas, I have not obtained it up to the present. Perhaps we may bring it forth, Allah Most High willing. I copied the entire book in a very brief period from the handwriting of its author. May Allah bless the most noble of His creation, our master Muhammad, and his family and Companions, and grant them abundant peace. Amen.’

“The writing of it was completed on the blessed Saturday, the thirteenth of the month of Dhu al-Hijjah, in the year 1129 after the Prophetic Hijra—upon him who ennobled it be the best blessings and peace. It was written in his own hand by the servant in need of the pardon of his Lord, the needy Muhammad ibn the learned shaykh, Shaykh Hadir, ibn the late Shaykh Abd Allah ibn the late Shaykh Ahmad al-Damhawhi al-Shafi'i. May Allah forgive him and his father.”

unresolved.explanation: The phrase is grammatically incomplete and ends with an explicit ellipsis. No supplied witness contains the colophon, so the missing relationship among “we,” “him,” and “whoever looks into it” cannot be recovered safely. The English preserves the fragment literally.

The construction is awkward, and the witnesses do not establish whether بالتحقيق is adverbial or reflects a textual disturbance. “Upon verification” is the most conservative contextual rendering, but the precise construction remains uncertain.

unresolved.arabic_span: وقد بقي عليه المبهمات، وقيد كثيرا منهما، والكنى لم أظفر به إلى الآن
unresolved.explanation: The referents of the dual منهما are not supplied, while the following plural الكنى is resumed by singular به. No relevant witness resolves the wording. The translation therefore retains “the two of them” and the singular “it.”
The unvocalized spelling supports the mechanical form al-Wandi, but the supplied evidence does not establish its historical pronunciation or identification.
Hadir is a reasonable mechanical transliteration, but the unvocalized Arabic and unrelated witnesses do not establish the precise pronunciation.
Al-Damhawhi mechanically represents the canonical consonantal spelling, but its precise vocalization and identification cannot be established from the supplied evidence.
